cues.en: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢。

cues.en: When I was a boy, my parents would sometimes take me camping in California.
cues.zh: 我小时候，父母有时会带我去加利福尼亚露营。

cues.en: We would camp in the beaches, in the forests, in the deserts.
cues.zh: 我们会在海滩、森林和沙漠里扎营。

cues.en: Some people think the deserts are empty of life, but my parents taught me to see the wildlife all around us,
cues.zh: 有些人觉得沙漠里没有生命，但我父母教会我去发现身边各处的野生动物，

cues.en: the hawks, the eagles,
cues.zh: 鹰、雕，

cues.en: the tortoises.
cues.zh: 还有陆龟。

cues.en: One time when we were setting up camp,
cues.zh: 有一次我们正在搭帐篷，

cues.en: we found a baby scorpion with its stinger out, and I remember thinking how cool it was that something could be both so cute and also so dangerous.
cues.zh: 发现了一只翘着毒刺的小蝎子，我记得当时觉得特别酷——一个东西竟然能既这么可爱，又这么危险。

cues.en: After college, I moved to California, I started working on a number of environmental campaigns.
cues.zh: 大学毕业后，我搬到加州，开始参与一系列环保运动。

cues.en: I got involved in helping to save the state's last ancient redwood forest and blocking a proposed radioactive waste repository
cues.zh: 我参与拯救该州最后一片古老红杉林，并阻止一个拟建的放射性废物处置库

cues.en: set for the desert. Shortly after I turned 30, I decided I wanted to dedicate a significant amount of my life to solving climate change. I was worried that global warming would end up destroying
cues.zh: 选址在沙漠。刚过30岁不久，我决定把人生中相当大的一部分投入到解决气候变化上。我担心全球变暖最终会摧毁

cues.en: many of the natural environments that people had worked so hard to protect.
cues.zh: 人们曾努力保护的许多自然环境。

cues.en: I thought the technical solutions were pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 我原以为技术方案已经相当明确了。

cues.en: Solar panels on every roof, electric car in the driveway, that the main obstacles were political.
cues.zh: 每栋屋顶都装太阳能板，车道上停着电动车，主要障碍在于政治。

cues.en: And so I helped to organize a coalition of the country's biggest labor unions and biggest environmental groups.
cues.zh: 于是我协助组织了一个联盟，把全国最大的几家工会和最大的环保团体联合起来。

cues.en: Our proposal was for a $300,000,000,000
cues.zh: 我们的提案是投入 3000 亿美元

cues.en: investment in renewables.
cues.zh: 用于可再生能源。

cues.en: And the idea was not only would we prevent climate change, but we would also create millions of new jobs in a very fast growing high-tech sector.
cues.zh: 我们的设想是，这不仅能阻止气候变化，还能在一个高速增长的高科技领域创造数百万个新岗位。

cues.en: Our efforts really paid off in 2007
cues.zh: 我们的努力在2007年真正得到了回报

cues.en: when then presidential candidate Barack Obama embraced our vision. Between 2009 and 2015,
cues.zh: 当时还是总统候选人的Barack Obama接受了我们的愿景。2009年到2015年间，

cues.en: The US invested a $150,000,000,000
cues.zh: 美国投入了1500亿美元

cues.en: in renewables and other kinds of clean tech.
cues.zh: 用于可再生能源和其他类型的清洁技术。

cues.en: But right away, we started to encounter some problems. First of all, the electricity from solar rooftops
cues.zh: 但我们很快就遇到了一些问题。首先，屋顶太阳能发的电

cues.en: ends up costing about twice as much as the electricity from solar farms.
cues.zh: 最终成本大约是太阳能农场发电的两倍。

cues.en: And both solar farms and wind farms require covering a pretty significant amount of land with solar panels and wind turbines,
cues.zh: 而且太阳能农场和风电场都需要占用大量土地来铺设太阳能板和安装风力涡轮机，

cues.en: and also building very big transmission lines to bring all electricity from the countryside into the city.
cues.zh: 还需要建设非常大型的输电线路，把乡村的电力全部输送到城市。

cues.en: Both of those things were often very strongly resisted by local communities
cues.zh: 这两件事常常遭到当地社区的强烈抵制

cues.en: as well as by conservation biologists who were concerned about the impacts on wild bird species and other animals.
cues.zh: 也遭到保护生物学家的强烈抵制，他们担心会对野生鸟类及其他动物造成影响。

cues.en: Now, there was a lot of other people working on technical solutions at the time. One of the big challenges, of course, is just the intermittency of solar and wind. They only generate electricity about 10 to 30% of the time during most of the year. But some of the solutions that were being proposed were to convert hydroelectric
cues.zh: 当时还有很多其他人在研究技术解决方案。当然，一大挑战就是太阳能和风能的间歇性。在一年的大部分时间里，它们只有约10%到30%的时间在发电。但当时提出的一些解决方案，是把水电

cues.en: dams into gigantic batteries.
cues.zh: 大坝改造成巨型电池。

cues.en: The idea was that when the sun was shining and the wind was blowing, you would pump the water uphill,
cues.zh: 这个想法是，当阳光充足、风吹起来时，就把水抽到高处，

cues.en: store it for later, and then when you needed electricity, run it over the turbines.
cues.zh: 储存起来备用，等需要用电时，再让水流过水轮机发电。

cues.en: In terms of wildlife, some of these problems just didn't seem like a significant concern. So when I learned that house cats kill billions of birds every year, it put into perspective the hundreds of thousands of birds, rather, that that are killed by wind turbines.
cues.zh: 就野生动物而言，其中一些问题似乎并不值得严重担忧。所以当我得知家猫每年杀死数十亿只鸟时，这让我对风电机杀死的数十万只鸟——更确切地说，是每年被风电机杀死的鸟——有了更客观的认识。

cues.en: It basically seemed to me at the time that most, if not all, of the problems of scaling up solar and wind could be solved through more technological
cues.zh: 当时在我看来，扩大太阳能和风能规模的问题，即便不是全部，也大多能靠更多的技术

cues.en: innovation.
cues.zh: 创新来解决。

cues.en: But as the years went by, these problems persisted and in many cases grew worse.
cues.zh: 但几年过去，这些问题依然存在，很多情况下还变得更糟。

cues.en: So California is a state that's really committed to renewable energy, but we still haven't converted many of our hydroelectric dams into big batteries.
cues.zh: 加州确实非常致力于可再生能源，但我们还没把多少水电站改造成大型电池。

cues.en: Some of the problems are just geographic.
cues.zh: 有些问题纯粹是地理上的。

cues.en: It's just you have to have a very particular kind of formation to be able to do that. And even in those cases, it's quite expensive to make those conversions.
cues.zh: 只是你必须具备非常特殊的构造才能做到。而且即便在这种情况下，进行这些转化也相当昂贵。

cues.en: Other challenges are just that there's other uses for water, like irrigation.
cues.zh: 其他挑战在于，水还有其他用途，比如灌溉。

cues.en: And maybe this is the most significant problem, is just that in California,
cues.zh: 也许这是最重要的问题，那就是在加利福尼亚，

cues.en: the water in our rivers and reservoirs
cues.zh: 我们河流和水库中的水

cues.en: is growing increasingly
cues.zh: 正变得越来越

cues.en: scarce and unreliable due to climate change.
cues.zh: 稀缺且不可靠，因为气候变化。

cues.en: In terms of this issue of of reliability,
cues.zh: 就可靠性这个问题而言，

cues.en: as as a consequence of it, we've actually had to stop the electricity coming from the solar farms into the cities because there's just been too much of it at times, or we've been starting to pay our neighboring states like Arizona to take that solar electricity. The alternative is to suffer from blowouts of the grid.
cues.zh: 因此，我们实际上不得不停止太阳能电站向城市输电，因为有时电力实在太多，或者我们开始付钱给亚利桑那等邻州，让他们接收这些太阳能电力。替代方案就是承受电网过载崩溃。

cues.en: And it it turns out that when it comes to birds and cats,
cues.zh: 而事实证明，说到鸟类和猫，

cues.en: cats don't kill eagles.
cues.zh: 猫不会捕杀鹰。

cues.en: Eagles kill cats.
cues.zh: 鹰会杀死猫。

cues.en: What cats kill are the small common
cues.zh: 猫杀死的是那些小型常见的

cues.en: sparrows and jays and robins, birds that are not endangered and not at risk of going extinct.
cues.zh: 麻雀、松鸦和知更鸟，这些鸟并未濒危，也没有灭绝风险。

cues.en: What
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: what do kill eagles and other big birds like this kite,
cues.zh: 杀死鹰以及像这只鸢这样的大型鸟类的，

cues.en: as well as owls and condors and other threatened and endangered species,
cues.zh: 还有猫头鹰、神鹰和其他受威胁、濒危物种的，

cues.en: are wind turbines. In fact, they're one of the most significant threats to those big bird species that we have. We just haven't been introducing the airspace with many other objects like we have wind turbines over the last several years.
cues.zh: 是风力发电机。事实上，它们是我们所拥有的那些大型鸟类物种面临的最重大威胁之一。过去几年，我们只是一直没有像引入风力发电机那样，把许多其他物体引入这片空域。

cues.en: And in terms of solar,
cues.zh: 说到太阳能，

cues.en: you know, building a solar farm is a lot like building any other kind of farm. You have to clear the whole area of wildlife.
cues.zh: 建太阳能农场很像建其他任何农场。你得把整个区域的野生动物清走。

cues.en: So this is a picture of one third of
cues.zh: 这是一张照片，展示的是三分之一

cues.en: one of the biggest solar farms in California called Ivanpah.
cues.zh: 加州最大太阳能农场之一，叫 Ivanpah。

cues.en: In order to build this, they had to clear the whole area of desert tortoises, literally pulling desert tortoises
cues.zh: 为了建它，他们得把整片区域的沙漠陆龟清走，硬生生把沙漠陆龟

cues.en: and their babies out of burrows,
cues.zh: 和它们的幼龟从洞穴里拽出来，

cues.en: putting them on the back of pickup trucks and transporting them to captivity,
cues.zh: 放上皮卡车后斗，运到圈养地，

cues.en: where many of them ended up dying. And currently, the current estimates are that about 6,000 birds are killed every year, actually catching on fire above the solar farm and and plunging to their deaths. Over time, it gradually struck me that there was really no amount of technological innovation that was gonna make the sun shine more regularly or wind blow more reliably.
cues.zh: 其中很多最后都死了。而目前估计，每年约有 6000 只鸟死亡，它们实际上是在太阳能农场上空着火，然后坠亡。随着时间推移，我逐渐意识到，再多的技术创新，也真的无法让太阳更规律地照耀，或让风更可靠地吹。

cues.en: In fact, nothing could... You could make solar panels cheaper, you could make wind turbines bigger, but sunlight and wind are just really dilute fuels. And in order to produce significant amounts of electricity,
cues.zh: 事实上，没什么能……你可以让太阳能板更便宜，让风机更大，但阳光和风本来就是非常稀薄的燃料。而要产生大量电力，

cues.en: you just have to cover a very large landmass with them. In other words,
cues.zh: 你就得用它们覆盖非常大的一片陆地。换句话说，

cues.en: all of the major problems with renewables
cues.zh: 可再生能源的所有主要问题

cues.en: aren't technical,
cues.zh: 都不是技术问题，

cues.en: they're natural.
cues.zh: 而是自然条件问题。

cues.en: Well, dealing with all of this unreliability
cues.zh: 那么，要应对所有这些不可靠性

cues.en: and the big environmental impacts obviously comes at a pretty high economic cost. You know, we've been hearing a lot about how solar panels and wind turbines have come down in cost in recent years, but that cost has been significantly
cues.zh: 以及巨大的环境影响，显然都要付出相当高的经济代价。你知道，我们近年常听说太阳能板和风机成本降了很多，但成本下降带来的好处，已经被显著

cues.en: outweighed
cues.zh: 抵消了——

cues.en: by just the challenges of integrating all of that unreliable power onto the grid. Just take for instance what's happened in California.
cues.zh: 仅仅是把所有这些不可靠的电力并入电网的挑战。就拿加州发生的事来说。

cues.en: At the period in which solar panels have come down in price very significantly, same with wind, we've seen our electricity prices go up five times more than the rest of the country,
cues.zh: 在太阳能板价格大幅下降、风能也是如此的时期，我们的电价涨幅却是全国其他地区的五倍多，

cues.en: and it... It's not unique to us. You can see the same phenomenon happened in Germany, which is really the world's leader in solar, wind, and other renewable technologies.
cues.zh: 而且这……这不只是我们。你能看到同样的现象也发生在德国，而德国确实是太阳能、风能和其他可再生能源技术的世界领先者。

cues.en: Their prices increased 50%
cues.zh: 他们的电价上涨了50%

cues.en: during their big renewable energy push. Now, you might think, well,
cues.zh: 在他们大力推进可再生能源的期间。现在，你可能会想，好吧，

cues.en: dealing with climate change is just going to require that we all pay more for energy. That's what I used to think. But consider the case of France.
cues.zh: 应对气候变化只会要求我们所有人支付更高的能源费用。我以前也这么想。但看看法国的例子。

cues.en: France actually gets twice as much of its electricity from clean zero emission sources than does Germany,
cues.zh: 法国来自清洁零排放能源的电力其实是德国的两倍，

cues.en: and yet France pays
cues.zh: 然而法国却要支付

cues.en: half as much, almost half as much for its electricity.
cues.zh: 一半，几乎一半的电费。

cues.en: How can that be? Well, you might have already anticipated the answer. France gets most of its electricity from nuclear power, about 75%
cues.zh: 怎么会这样？你可能已经猜到答案了。法国大部分电力来自核电，约占75%

cues.en: in total. Nuclear just ends up being a lot more reliable,
cues.zh: 的总量。核电最终可靠得多，

cues.en: generating power twenty four hours a day, seven days a week, for about 90% of the year.
cues.zh: 一年约90%的时间都能每周7天、每天24小时发电。

cues.en: We see this phenomenon show up at a global level. For example, there's been a natural experiment over the last forty years, even more than that, in terms of the deployment of nuclear and the deployment of solar.
cues.zh: 我们能在全球层面看到这一现象。例如，过去四十年来，甚至更长时间里，在核能和太阳能的部署方面，出现了一场自然实验。

cues.en: You can see that
cues.zh: 可以看到

cues.en: at a little bit higher cost, we got about half as much electricity from solar and wind than we did from nuclear.
cues.zh: 成本略高一些，我们从太阳能和风能获得的电力却只有核能的大约一半。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: what does all this mean for going forward? I think one of the most significant findings to date is this one. Had Germany spent $580,000,000,000
cues.zh: 这一切对今后意味着什么？我认为迄今最重要的发现之一是这个：如果德国把 5800 亿美元

cues.en: on nuclear instead of renewables,
cues.zh: 投在核能而不是可再生能源上，

cues.en: it would already be getting a 100% of its of its electricity from clean energy sources
cues.zh: 那它现在已经能从清洁能源获得 100% 的电力

cues.en: and all of its transportation energy.
cues.zh: 以及全部交通能源。

cues.en: Now, I think you might be wondering, and it's quite reasonable to ask, is nuclear power safe and what do you do with the waste? Well, those are very reasonable questions. Turns out that there's been scientific studies on this going over forty years. This is just the most recent study that was done by the prestigious British medical journal Lancet, finds that nuclear power is the safest.
cues.zh: 现在，你可能会想，而且也很该问：核能安全吗？废料怎么处理？这些问题都很合理。事实证明，这方面的科学研究已经持续了四十多年。这只是权威英国医学期刊《柳叶刀》最新完成的一项研究，其结论是核能最安全。

cues.en: It's easy to understand why.
cues.zh: 原因很容易理解。

cues.en: According to the World Health Organization, about seven million people die annually from air pollution, and nuclear plants don't emit that. As a result, the climate scientist James Hansen looked at it and he calculated that nuclear power has already saved almost two million lives to date.
cues.zh: 根据世界卫生组织的数据，每年约有七百万人死于空气污染，而核电站不会排放这些污染物。因此，气候科学家 James Hansen 研究后计算出，迄今为止核电已经挽救了近两百万人的生命。

cues.en: It turns out that even wind energy is more deadly than nuclear.
cues.zh: 事实证明，就连风能的致死性也比核能更高。

cues.en: This is a photograph
cues.zh: 这是一张照片

cues.en: taken of two maintenance workers in The Netherlands shortly before one of them fell to his death to avoid the fire and the other one was engulfed in flames.
cues.zh: 拍的是荷兰的两名维修工人，就在不久后，其中一人为避火坠落身亡，另一人则被火焰吞没。

cues.en: Now, what about environmental impact?
cues.zh: 那环境影响呢？

cues.en: I think a really easy way to think about it is that uranium fuel, which is what we use to power nuclear plants, is just really energy dense. About the
cues.zh: 我觉得很好理解的一点是：我们用来驱动核电站的铀燃料，能量密度真的很高。大约

cues.en: same amount of uranium as this
cues.zh: 和这个

cues.en: Rubik's cube can power all of the energy that you need in your entire life.
cues.zh: 魔方一样多的铀，就能提供你一生所需的全部能量。

cues.en: As a consequence, you just don't need that much land in order to produce a significant amount of electricity.
cues.zh: 因此，要发出可观的电力，你并不需要占用那么多土地。

cues.en: Here, you can compare the solar farm I just described, Ivanpah, to California's
cues.zh: 在这里，你可以把我刚描述的那座太阳能农场 Ivanpah 与加利福尼亚的作比较

cues.en: last nuclear plant, Diablo Canyon. It takes 450
cues.zh: 最后一座核电站，Diablo Canyon。它需要 450

cues.en: times more land to generate the same amount of electricity
cues.zh: 需要多出数倍的土地才能发出同等电量

cues.en: as it does from nuclear.
cues.zh: 正如它从核能中获取一样。

cues.en: You would need 17 more solar farms like Ivanpaw
cues.zh: 你需要再建17个像 Ivanpaw 那样的太阳能农场。

cues.en: in order to generate the same output as Diablo Canyon, and of course, it would then be unreliable.
cues.zh: 为了得到和 Diablo Canyon 相同的输出，当然，那样它就会变得不可靠。

cues.en: Well, what about the mining and the waste and the material throughput?
cues.zh: 嗯，那采矿、废弃物和物料吞吐量呢？

cues.en: Well, this has been studied pretty closely as well, and it just turns out that solar panels require 17 times more materials than nuclear plants do in the form of cement, glass, concrete, steel, and that includes all the fuel used for those nuclear plants.
cues.zh: 这一点也已经被相当仔细地研究过，结果发现：太阳能板所需的水泥、玻璃、混凝土、钢材等材料是核电站的 17 倍，而且这还包括核电站使用的全部燃料。

cues.en: The consequence is that what comes out at the end, since it's material throughput, is just not a lot of waste from nuclear.
cues.zh: 所以最终算下来，由于看的是材料吞吐量，核能产生的废料其实并不多。

cues.en: All of the waste from the Swiss nuclear program fits into this room. Nuclear waste is actually the only waste from electricity production that's safely contained and internalized.
cues.zh: 瑞士核计划产生的所有废料都能装进这个房间。核废料实际上是电力生产中唯一被安全封存并内部化处理的废物。

cues.en: Every other way of making electricity emits the waste into the natural environment, either as pollution
cues.zh: 其他所有发电方式都会把废料排入自然环境，要么作为污染

cues.en: or as material waste.
cues.zh: 要么作为材料废料。

cues.en: We tend to think of solar panels as clean,
cues.zh: 我们往往认为太阳能电池板很清洁，

cues.en: but the truth is that there is no plan to deal with solar panels at the end of their twenty or twenty five year life. A lot of experts are actually very concerned that solar panels are just going to be shipped to poor countries in Africa or Asia with the rest of our electronic waste stream to be disassembled,
cues.zh: 但事实是，太阳能电池板在20或25年寿命结束后，根本没有处理方案。很多专家其实非常担心，太阳能电池板会和其他电子垃圾一起被运往非洲或亚洲的贫困国家进行拆解，

cues.en: often exposing people to really high levels of toxic elements
cues.zh: 常常让人们暴露在极高浓度的有毒元素中

cues.en: including lead, cadmium, and chromium, elements that, because they're elements,
cues.zh: 包括铅、镉和铬，这些元素因为是元素，

cues.en: their toxicity never declines over time. I think we have an intuitive sense that nuclear is a really powerful, strong energy source and that sunlight is really dilute and diffuse and weak, which is why you have to spread solar collectors or wind collectors over such a large amount of land.
cues.zh: 其毒性永远不会随时间下降。我觉得我们有一种直觉：核能是极其强大、强劲的能源，而阳光非常稀薄、分散、微弱，这就是为什么必须把太阳能收集器或风力收集器铺在如此大面积的土地上。

cues.en: Maybe that's why nobody was surprised when, in the recent science fiction remake of Blade Runner, the film opens in a very dark dystopian scene where California's deserts have been entirely paved with solar farms.
cues.zh: 也许这就是为什么，在最近那部科幻翻拍片 Blade Runner 中，没人感到惊讶：影片开场就是一个非常黑暗的反乌托邦场景，加利福尼亚的沙漠全被太阳能农场铺满了。

cues.en: All of which I think raises a really uncomfortable question.
cues.zh: 我认为这一切引出了一个非常令人不安的问题。

cues.en: In the effort to try to save the climate,
cues.zh: 为了努力拯救气候，

cues.en: are we destroying the environment?
cues.zh: 我们是否正在破坏环境？

cues.en: Well, the interesting thing is that over the last several hundred years, human beings have actually been trying to move away from what you would consider matter dense fuels towards energy dense ones. That means really from wood and dung towards coal, oil, natural gas, uranium. This is a phenomenon that's been going on for a long time. Poor countries around the world are in the process still of moving away from wood and dung as their primary energies. And for the most part, this is a positive thing.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，过去几百年里，人类其实一直在努力摆脱所谓物质密集的燃料，转向能量密集的燃料。也就是从木材和粪便转向煤炭、石油、天然气、铀。这个现象已经持续很久了。世界各地的贫困国家仍在逐步摆脱以木材和粪便作为主要能源。而且总体来看，这是件好事。

cues.en: As you stop using wood as your major source of fuel, it allows the forest to grow back and the wildlife to return. As you stop burning wood in your home, you don't... You no longer need to breathe that toxic smoke. And as you go from coal to natural gas and uranium as your main sources of energy, it holds out the possibility of basically eliminating air pollution altogether.
cues.zh: 当你不再把木材作为主要燃料来源，森林就能重新长回来，野生动物也会回归。当你在家里不再烧木柴时，你就不……你不再需要吸入那种有毒烟雾。而当你从煤炭转向天然气和铀作为主要能源时，这就有可能基本上彻底消除空气污染。

cues.en: There's just this problem with nuclear. While it's been pretty popular to move from dirtier to cleaner energy sources, from energy diffused to energy dense sources, nuclear is just really unpopular for a bunch of historical reasons.
cues.zh: 核能就是有这个问题。尽管从更脏的能源转向更清洁的能源、从能量分散的能源转向能量密集的能源一直相当受欢迎，但由于一堆历史原因，核能就是非常不受欢迎。

cues.en: And as a consequence,
cues.zh: 因此，

cues.en: in the past, I and I think a lot of others have sort of said, well, in order to deal with climate change, we're just going to need all the different kinds of clean energy that we have. The problem is that just turns out not to be true. You remember I discussed France a little bit ago. France gets most of its electricity from nuclear.
cues.zh: 过去，我和我认为很多其他人多少都说过：要应对气候变化，我们就需要所有不同类型的清洁能源。问题是，事实证明这并不成立。你还记得我刚才稍微提到过法国吧。法国大部分电力来自核能。

cues.en: If France were to try to significantly
cues.zh: 如果法国想要大幅

cues.en: scale up solar and wind, it would also have to significantly reduce how much electricity it gets from nuclear.
cues.zh: 扩大太阳能和风能，它也就必须大幅减少从核能获得的电力。

cues.en: That's because in order to handle the huge variability of solar and wind on the grid, they would need to burn more natural gas. Think of it this way, it's just really hard to ramp up and down a nuclear plant, whereas I think we're all pretty familiar with turning the natural gas up and down on our stove. A similar process works in managing the grid. Of course, it goes without saying that oil and gas companies understand this pretty well, which is why we've seen them invest millions of dollars in recent years in promoting solar and wind.
cues.zh: 这是因为要应对电网中太阳能和风能的巨大波动，他们就得烧更多天然气。可以这么想：核电站的功率升降真的很难，而我们大家应该都很熟悉在炉灶上把天然气调大调小。管理电网也是类似的道理。当然，不用说，石油和天然气公司对此非常清楚，所以近年来我们看到它们投入数百万美元推广太阳能和风能。

cues.en: This just raises, I think, another challenging
cues.zh: 我认为，这只是引出了另一个棘手的

cues.en: question, which is that in places that are using a lot of nuclear, have grids that are mostly
cues.zh: 问题，那就是，在大量使用核能的地方，电网主要

cues.en: nuclear and hydro,
cues.zh: 依靠核能和水电，

cues.en: going towards solar and wind and other renewables
cues.zh: 转向太阳能、风能和其他可再生能源

cues.en: would actually increase carbon emissions.
cues.zh: 实际上会增加碳排放。

cues.en: I think a better alternative is just to tell the truth, and that's what a number of scientists have been doing. I mentioned earlier that
cues.zh: 我认为更好的做法就是说出真相，而这也是不少科学家一直在做的。我之前提到过

cues.en: hundreds of thousands of birds are killed every year by wind turbines. What I didn't mention is that a million bats, at a minimum, are killed every year by wind. The consequence has been that bat scientists have been speaking out about this. This particular bat species, the hoary bat, which is a migratory bat species, is literally at risk of going extinct right now because of the significant expansion of wind.
cues.zh: 每年有数十万只鸟被风力涡轮机杀死。我没提到的是，每年至少有上百万只蝙蝠被风电杀死。结果是，研究蝙蝠的科学家一直在公开谈论这件事。这种蝙蝠——灰蝙蝠，是一种迁徙性蝙蝠——由于风电的大规模扩张，现在真的面临灭绝风险。

cues.en: It's not just wind, it's also on solar. The scientists who were involved in creating the Ivanpah Solar farm, who were involved in clearing that land, have been speaking out.
cues.zh: 不只是风能，太阳能也一样。参与创建Ivanpah太阳能农场、参与清理那片土地的科学家们，一直在公开发声。

cues.en: One of them wrote, Everybody knows that translocation
cues.zh: 其中一人写道：大家都知道，迁地

cues.en: of desert tortoises doesn't work. When you're walking in front of a bulldozer crying and moving animals and cacti out of the way, it's hard to think that the project is a good idea.
cues.zh: 对沙漠陆龟行不通。当你走在推土机前，哭着把动物和仙人掌挪开时，很难觉得这个项目是个好主意。

cues.en: Now we can see these phenomena
cues.zh: 现在我们可以看到这些现象

cues.en: at work at an international level. In my home state of California,
cues.zh: 正在国际层面上起作用。在我的家乡加利福尼亚州，

cues.en: we've been stuffing a lot of natural gas into the side of a mountain in order to handle all that intermittent solar and wind. It sprung a leak. It was the equivalent to putting 500,000
cues.zh: 我们一直把大量天然气注入山体一侧，以应对那些间歇性的太阳能和风能。结果发生了泄漏。这相当于把50万

cues.en: cars on the road. And currently, in Germany, there's protesters trying to block a new coal mining project that would involve destroying the ancient Hombach Forest in order to get to the coal underneath,
cues.zh: 辆汽车开上道路。而目前，在德国，有抗议者试图阻止一个新的煤矿开采项目，该项目为了开采地下的煤，将涉及摧毁古老的Hombach Forest，

cues.en: all in an effort to phase out nuclear and expand solar and wind.
cues.zh: 这一切都是为了逐步淘汰核能，并扩大太阳能和风能。

cues.en: The good news is that
cues.zh: 好消息是

cues.en: I think that people still care about nature enough for these facts to matter.
cues.zh: 我认为人们仍然足够关心自然，这些事实才会有意义。

cues.en: We saw last year in South Korea, a citizen's jury deliberated for several months weighing these different issues. They had to decide whether they were going to phase out nuclear or or keep it and expand it. They started out 40%
cues.zh: 去年在韩国，我们看到一个公民陪审团花了几个月权衡这些不同问题。他们必须决定是逐步淘汰核能，还是保留并扩大核能。他们一开始有40%

cues.en: in favor of expanding nuclear, but after several months and considering these issues, they ended up voting 60%
cues.zh: 支持扩大核能，但经过数月并考虑这些问题后，他们最终投票有60%

cues.en: to expand nuclear. A similar phenomenon just happened last week in Arizona.
cues.zh: 支持扩大核能。上周在亚利桑那州也发生了类似现象。

cues.en: The voters had a ballot initiative that... To vote on whether or not to, continue with nuclear or to phase it out and try to replace it with natural gas and solar. They ended up rejecting it 70 to 30.
cues.zh: 选民们有一项公投提案……就是否继续使用核能，还是逐步淘汰核能并尝试用天然气和太阳能替代进行投票。最终他们以70比30否决了该提案。

cues.en: And even here in Europe, we saw The Netherlands is the... One of the first countries in recent memory to actually announce, as they did last week, that they're gonna start to they're gonna start to increase their reliance on nuclear power in recognition that there's just no way they could generate significant amounts of energy enough from solar and wind to meet their climate targets.
cues.zh: 即便在欧洲这里，我们也看到荷兰是……近来最早宣布的国家之一，正如他们上周所做的那样，他们将要开始增加对核电的依赖，因为他们认识到，仅靠太阳能和风能根本无法产生足够的能源来满足其气候目标。

cues.en: I think it's natural that those of us that became very concerned about climate change, such a big environmental issue,
cues.zh: 我认为，我们这些非常关注气候变化这一重大环境问题的人，自然会

cues.en: would gravitate towards really romantic solutions like harmonizing human civilization with the natural world using renewable energies.
cues.zh: 倾向于那些非常浪漫的解决方案，比如利用可再生能源让人类文明与自然世界和谐共处。

cues.en: But I think it's also understandable that as the facts have come in, that many of us have started to question our prior beliefs and change our minds.
cues.zh: 但我也觉得可以理解：随着事实逐渐明朗，我们中许多人开始质疑自己先前的信念，并改变想法。

cues.en: For me, question now is,
cues.zh: 对我来说，现在的问题是，

cues.en: now that we know that renewables can't save the planet, are we going to keep letting them destroy it? Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 既然我们知道可再生能源救不了地球，我们还要继续让它们毁掉地球吗？非常感谢。
